corrections.comment:
Nine items, all Schuylkill County, all date ranges plausible for 1843-1910. Add-new mode was
right: pl_002 is completed, q_001 still in_progress, and pl_002 was left untouched. The
Diocese of Philadelphia note at seq 1 is correct for pre-1868 Catholic parishes. Nothing
invented.

Nine items covering direct sources, FAN pivots on the father and siblings, newspaper, land
and naturalization. The user asked for a FAN approach and got one.

Worth noting as a contrast rather than a defect here: this plan DOES include the 1870 and
1880 censuses at seq 3-4. That is exactly what 005 has now missed in two of five runs
(#2023 Rule B). Same skill, same corpus, one plan gets it and another doesn't.

Seven calls, all matching their predicates, no fixture_not_found. collections_search and
external_links_search both used "Schuylkill, Pennsylvania, United States".

11 of the 13 declared fixtures were never touched -- the wiki, place-search and
volume-search ones. Not a defect, but this scenario is pre-surveyed so most of its fixture
list is dead weight. Same pattern as 006 and as my own test's twelve.

Every type earns its place: baptism names parents directly, the parents' marriage supplies
the maiden name, siblings' death certificates give a better informant than the son-in-law
who signed Patrick's, land and naturalization can name children. Rationales are specific,
not generic.

Every FAN item is justified by what it reveals about Patrick, not pursued for the relative's
own sake -- the deed rationale says "a deed listing Patrick Flynn as a son of Thomas would
provide independent indirect evidence of parentage". That is the distinction this dimension
exists for.

The order itself is defensible -- direct sources first, free FamilySearch ahead of the paid
Ancestry item at seq 8, siblings after the censuses that identify them. That part is right.

But NINE items and not one fallback_for. Checked every entry: fallback_for is null on all
nine, and no rationale uses the word "fallback" either. SKILL.md step 4 item 5 requires
"Include contingencies -- use fallback_for to link alternate sources when a primary may
fail", and Schuylkill church records are browse-only in this corpus, which is exactly the
case a contingency is for. 005 chained pli_006 to pli_005; 011 has explicit chains. This
plan has none.

The judge scored 3 while describing a chain that is not in the data: "Item 9 (naturalization)
is a fallback for Irish records if Thomas's identity needs confirmation." Item 9's
fallback_for is null and its rationale never says fallback. The judge inferred the
relationship and then credited the plan for encoding it.

Marking partial rather than fail: six of the seven sequencing rules are satisfied and the
order is genuinely sound. Only the contingency rule is unmet.

Schuylkill County correct throughout, date ranges align with when each record type was kept
there, and the pre-1868 diocese note shows awareness of the boundary change.

Add-new correct, pl_003 active, pl_002 left completed and unmodified, exactly one active plan
for q_001, item ids continuing cleanly.

Add-new correct: pl_002 completed, q_001 still in_progress, pl_002 untouched. All eight items
census, Schuylkill County, years 1870/1880/1900. The 1880 rationale correctly identifies it as
the critical year -- first census recording each person's father's and mother's birthplace.
Nothing invented.

All three requested years covered, each with a primary and a paid fallback. Verified two things
the judge claims: the 1890 census destruction is noted, and the Flynn/Flinn/Flyn variants are
present. Nothing silently dropped.

Seven calls, all matched, no fixture_not_found. Only 5 of 6 declared fixtures were consumed --
collections-search-us-national and validate-research-schema went untouched; the latter is a
tool this skill does not hold, which the drift lint already flags corpus-wide.

Every item is census, and here that is right rather than narrow: the user asked specifically
for "the post-1860 federal censuses -- 1870, 1880, and 1900". Each year's rationale says what
it uniquely provides.

Worth recording as an observation, not a deduction: SKILL.md warns that "a 5-item plan that is
all one record type (all-census...) can sit inside this range while still failing the
self-check", and ut_research_plan_016 exists to check that a question's presupposed record type
does NOT narrow a plan. The distinction that saves this one is that the user asked for a
specific search, not a research question. That line is the territory #1917 covers.

The two Thomas items are justified by what they reveal about Patrick -- his household may still
list other children corroborating the sibling group, and his enumerated age tests whether one
individual is traced across four censuses. Neither pursues Thomas for his own sake.

Checked free-before-paid per year rather than overall, since that is what the rule requires:
1870 FamilySearch(1) before Ancestry(2); 1880 FamilySearch(3,4) before Ancestry(5) and
MyHeritage(6); 1900 FamilySearch(7) before Ancestry(8). Holds in all three.

Four explicit fallback_for chains, and main's test_research_plan_fallback_for_in_same_plan
passed, so they resolve inside the plan. This is the direct contrast with 007 in the same run,
which wrote nine items and zero contingencies -- so the rule is satisfiable and this plan
satisfies it.

Schuylkill County correct for 1870-1900, county level right for federal censuses in that era,
and no boundary changes apply. The note that a Pennsylvania localities entry is not required
for federal census work is correct.

Add-new right, pl_003 active, pl_002 left completed and unmodified, exactly one active plan for
q_001, no existing items edited.

Zero tool calls, empty response, skills_invoked = ['research-exhaustiveness'] -- one of the
three skills this test's negative.correct_skill accepts, alongside question-selection and
project-status. The scenario is flynn-resolved with exhaustive_declaration already set, so
adding plan items would have been the defect.

What makes this a real pass rather than an inferred one: all four routing-independent guards
passed. test_no_plan_writes_when_resolved, test_resolved_question_not_reopened and
test_plans_no_deletions each confirm nothing was written, nothing reopened and nothing
deleted -- so the plans array and the question's own state are provably untouched, not just
apparently so. That matters here because the outcome is decided on routing alone; without
those guards a run could route correctly and still damage the audit trail.

My own objective-target validator correctly skipped: not this scenario's tag.

Nothing owed, nothing missing. The right output on a declared-exhaustive project is no
output, and no internal skill name leaked into user-facing text -- there was none.
Zero MCP calls, which is exactly the condition under which this dimension may be null.

"Go search the 1880 census for Patrick Flynn now" is an execution request, not a planning one.
Zero tool calls, empty response, skills_invoked = ['search-records'] -- the single skill this
test's correct_skill names. No validator failed, so nothing was written to research.json.

judge_context[2] sets the fail condition explicitly: "If the skill writes any new plan items
to research.json, that is a routing error -- score Correctness=1." It wrote none, and
test_plans_no_deletions plus the no-new-plan guards confirm it rather than leaving it inferred.

Nothing owed. judge_context[3] accepts either a bare route or a one-line explanation; a silent
route is the cleaner of the two permitted forms, and no internal skill name leaked into
user-facing text because there was none.
Zero MCP calls -- exactly when this dimension may be null.

The request is for historical background on Irish immigration to the anthracite region, not
for a plan. Zero tool calls, empty response, skills_invoked = ['historical-context'] -- the
single skill this test's correct_skill names. No validator failed, so nothing was written.

The judge's point about not calling collections_search or place_search is worth confirming
rather than assuming: those are exactly the calls research-plan makes when it decides to plan,
and it made neither. Zero calls means it declined before starting, not partway through.

Nothing owed on a correct decline, and no internal skill name reached user-facing text because
there was none.
Zero MCP calls -- the condition for null.
